items.summary: Input/Output types on every function at every layer
items.details: Non-negotiable. Every orchestrator method, every repository method, every service method has *Input and *Output types. Never accept positional args. Never return bare types. Even helpers should use this pattern. This enables adding fields without breaking callers and future pagination.

items.summary: No proto types past the handler boundary
items.details: Handlers import and use pb. types for conversion. Orchestrators speak internal entity types ONLY. No pb. imports in orchestrators, services, repositories, or entity files. If a type needs to flow past the handler, define a local entity struct for it. The encounter orchestrator currently violates this — 39 pb. refs in orchestrator.go and 3 in service.go. These are tracked violations, not approved patterns.

items.summary: Test suites with gomock at interface boundaries
items.details: Use testify/suite for all test organization. Use go.uber.org/mock (gomock) for mocking at interface boundaries — not mockery. Place mocks in mock/ subdirectory next to the interface, using package name <domain>mock. Regenerate with go:generate.
Every New() or NewX() constructor validates its Config struct. If a required dependency is nil, return an error immediately. Never nil-check at runtime in methods. Fail fast at startup.
Every function returns either a valid non-nil output or an error. Empty results use empty structs or empty slices, not nil. This applies at every layer.

items.summary: Auth context extraction at handler, passed explicitly to orchestrator
items.details: Handlers call auth.PlayerIDFromContext(ctx) and pass playerID as a field in the orchestrator's input struct. The orchestrator does not access the context for auth. This keeps auth logic in one layer.

items.summary: Outside-in development: handler stub → interface → tests → implementation → repository
items.details: Start with a gRPC handler returning codes.Unimplemented. Define the service interface and Input/Output types. Write handler tests with mocked service. Implement the orchestrator. Implement the repository last. See docs/how-to/add-handler-method.md.

items.summary: Load-then-stream pattern for real-time encounter state
items.details: Clients call GetEncounterState to get a full snapshot with LastEventID, then call StreamEncounterEvents with last_event_id to receive only new events. The orchestrator updates LastEventID in EncounterData whenever an event is published. This is the canonical multi-player state sync pattern.

items.summary: Game logic belongs in rpg-toolkit, not rpg-api
items.details: If code checks weapon properties, calculates modifiers, evaluates conditions, or implements D&D rules — it belongs in rpg-toolkit. rpg-api passes entities to toolkit functions and persists results. The dungeon component is currently violating this boundary and is scheduled for migration.

items.summary: make pre-commit before every commit; make ci-check before every push
items.details: pre-commit runs: fmt, tidy, fix-eof, lint, test. ci-check runs scripts/ci-checks.sh for CI-specific validations. Never use --no-verify. If pre-commit fails, fix the issue — CI will fail with the same checks.

items.summary: Apply room origin at the merge boundary; cumulative encounter state is dungeon-absolute
items.details:
When folding revealed-room data (walls, entities, obstacles, monster placements) into cumulative encounter state, translate from room-local to dungeon-absolute at the producer using dungeon.Module.LocalToAbsolute (or the localToAbsoluteOrLocal helper in orchestrator.go for the single-room start case). Do this at the OpenDoor merge site, not at downstream consumers.

Producers that write to cumulative state and must apply origin:
- buildRoomLayoutProto (orchestrator.go ~1098): walls in EncounterStateData.rooms[].walls.
- localToAbsoluteOrLocal at OpenDoor (~3172): monster.Position in MonsterInfo / Entities map.
- buildCombinedRoomDataAfterOpenDoor (~5836): obstacle.Position in spatial.RoomData.CubeEntities.

Consumers (handlers, event publishers, perception, movement-collision, roomContainingPosition) treat cumulative state as already-absolute and never re-translate. The proto RoomLayout.Origin field is still emitted alongside absolute walls so a client can recover the local frame by subtraction if needed.

If you add a new producer of cumulative state and skip origin translation, you reproduce issue #493. Enforce this at code review for any new merge site.

items.summary: Wall consumers load the union of all revealed rooms' walls in dungeon-absolute, not just currentRoom.Walls
items.details:
Issue #465 (wall-consumer scope, separate from the type-unification scope tracked under the same issue number). Before this rule, every wall-aware path in the encounter orchestrator wrote a snippet like:

  if currentRoom := dungeon.GetRoom(currentRoomID); currentRoom != nil {
      dungeonWalls = currentRoom.Walls
  }

That is wrong any time more than one room is revealed. Once the player walks through OpenDoor, every other revealed room's perimeter is invisible to collision and to the wall set published in events.

The rule: use loadAbsoluteWallsForRevealedRooms(dng) in revealed_walls.go. It iterates dng.RevealedRooms, applies each room's origin (from dng.RoomOrigins) to every wall vertex element-wise, and returns the union in dungeon-absolute. The validator PathCrossesWall (and wallsToBlockedHexes for monster perception) is a 2D-segment-intersection / cube-rasterization function — frame-agnostic, so absolute-on-absolute works.

Consumers that must use the union:
- MoveCharacter (orchestrator.go ~1620): wall-collision check.
- executeMoveAction (orchestrator.go ~5290): wall-collision per path step.
- executeMonsterTurns (monster_turns.go ~50): perception BlockedHexes + validateMovementAgainstWalls.
- ResolveAttack (orchestrator.go ~520): AttackResolved event Walls field.
- EndTurn (orchestrator.go ~2065): TurnEnded / MonsterTurnCompleted event Walls field.

Door positions are passable by construction — perimeter generation (internal/components/dungeon/toolkit/perimeter.go) splits walls AROUND the door hex via createWallBeforeDoor / createWallAfterDoor, so the door is a gap in the wall list. No special-case logic needed in the collision check.

If you write a new consumer that calls dungeon.GetRoom(currentRoomID).Walls and treats that as the encounter wall set, you reproduce #465. Enforce this at code review.
